subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should later operator `tools.exec` security configuration be allowed to override or invalidate persisted per-session `/exec` host/security/ask/node values?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs deliberately preserve per-session `/exec` defaults, but the reported impact is that those persisted values can shadow a stricter later operator security policy.

options.title: Operator config wins
options.body: Treat stricter current config as authoritative and add migration/reset or doctor handling for existing session exec fields.

options.title: Preserve session defaults
options.body: Keep `/exec` as durable session state, but add explicit operator-facing audit/reset documentation or tooling so admins can clear stale overrides.

options.title: Leave current contract unchanged
options.body: Accept that `/exec` session state can outlive config changes and document tool-policy deny as the hard enforcement path.

recommendation.title: Operator config wins
recommendation.body: Treat stricter current config as authoritative and add migration/reset or doctor handling for existing session exec fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for the `/exec` session override contract and focused resolver tests points to steipete.
